subject: general
question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Still waters run deep

options.text: Desperate measures made in order to come out of a difficult situation
To have passion or great intelligence underneath a calm expression
To be confused or not understand something

solution:
The correct answer is** "To have passion or great intelligence underneath a calm expression."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 

__
 
• The phrase **"still waters run deep"** is an idiom that means a quiet or calm exterior often conceals a more complex or profound personality, intellect, or emotions. (एक शांत या शांत बाहरी भाग अक्सर अधिक जटिल या गहन व्यक्तित्व, बुद्धि या भावनाओं को छुपाता है)
 
• It suggests that someone who appears quiet, reserved, or unassuming on the surface may possess great depth, intelligence, or strong emotions underneath.
 
 
• **Example**:* John may seem quiet, but **still waters run deep**__.*
 
 
 
• It's often used to caution against underestimating or making assumptions about someone based solely on their outward appearance or demeanor.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
